subject: Archive slicing & on-demand extract procedures — Crescent Bank RFI
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <s.connors@crescentbank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Price <t.price@crescentbank.com>, compliance@crescentbank.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: on-demand export / retention scenarios and chain-of-custody requirements

David —

Thanks for taking this. We have an upcoming regulatory review and our internal audit is asking for a detailed description of how Redwood would deliver audit logs and event histories on demand in several scenarios:

- Full forensic harvest (ordered, complete events, O(100GB)) delivered within 48 hours.
- Incremental slices (e.g., 7-day windows) for targeted investigations.
- Redaction options for PII prior to handoff vs handing unredacted encrypted archives.
- Support for legal hold where data must be preserved and erasure requests deferred.

Please include: expected timelines for a 100–250 GB export, how you preserve ordering and provenance (checksums, manifests), your tamper-evidence or chain-of-custody proofs, and any constraints around cold/nearline data retrieval. Also call out what you can provide for subject access / GDPR erasure workflows tied to the same export tooling.

Attachments: Crescent_Retention_RFI_001.pdf (our questionnaire)

Appreciate a concise playbook and ETA so we can decide whether to include Redwood in the regulator packet.

— Sarah Connors
Head of Compliance, Crescent Bank
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <s.connors@crescentbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: on-demand export / retention scenarios and chain-of-custody requirements

Sarah —

Thanks for the detail. Looping in Neha (product/security) and Ben (ops) to provide a short, technical playbook and a sample manifest we can attach to your regulator package.

Quick answers up front:
- We can do full forensic harvests of 100–250 GB within 24–48 hours from hosted systems (SLA varies by region and Dedicated commitments).
- We produce a machine-readable manifest with sequence-range metadata, per-chunk checksums (SHA256), and a signed delivery receipt that includes time-synced hashes for tamper evidence.
- Incremental slices: supported; manifests include inclusive start/end timestamps and cursor tokens to resume exports.
- GDPR/erasure: erasure requests are handled at the tenant layer and can be coordinated with legal holds; when a legal hold is in place, erasure is deferred and marked in our retention ledger.

Neha / Ben — can you prepare the playbook (attachments: retention-matrix.xlsx, export_manifest_template.json) and a suggested timeline for 100GB/250GB delivery? Also include the standard checksums and custody language we provide to customers. I can review and send a single PDF back to Crescent.

Thanks,
David
Director, Customer Solutions

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

David / Ben —

Attached are the artifacts: retention-matrix.xlsx and export_manifest_template.json (draft). I also included a short PDF checklist (sample-handoff-checklist.pdf) for SOC2-style evidence. Key points in the draft:

- Export timelines (hosted): small (<10GB) within 4–8 hrs; medium (10–100GB) within 24 hrs; large (100–250GB) within 24–48 hrs. Dedicated customers with reserved capacity can commit to the lower bound.
- We produce chunked archives (default 10GB chunk size) with per-chunk SHA256 and an overall signed manifest (RSA-2048 signature tied to the delivery event).
- Ordering is preserved by including sequence_start and sequence_end and a global monotonic export cursor in the manifest. If required, we can also provide event offsets and session ids to reconstruct causal chains.
- Export formats: NDJSON for quick ingest, Parquet available for analytics-heavy handoffs. Both are compressed (gzip/snappy) and encrypted in transit via TLS 1.3; at-rest encryption on object storage uses customer-managed KMS if requested.
- GDPR / Legal hold: we surface hold state in the tenant control plane. Erasure requests submitted via our support/console will be blocked if an active legal hold exists; we log the hold and provide an auditable record with timestamps.
- Chain-of-custody: manifest + per-chunk checksums + signed delivery receipt + delivery timestamp. For additional forensic rigor we can produce an integrity statement stamped by our SRE on handoff.

I recommend sending this with two attachments (retention-matrix.xlsx, export_manifest_template.json) and an optional checklist PDF for regulators.

-Neha
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sarah / Tom —

Attached please find the requested playbook and technical appendix. Summary (high level):

1) Delivery timelines (hosted):
   - <10 GB: typical 4–8 hours
   - 10–100 GB: typical 24 hours
   - 100–250 GB: 24–48 hours (expedited with Dedicated commitment)

2) Provenance & tamper evidence:
   - Export is produced as chunked archives (default 10GB), each chunk includes a SHA256 checksum.
   - A signed manifest (export_manifest_template.json) lists chunk URIs, sequence ranges, inclusive timestamps, and a monotonic export cursor.
   - Delivery uses TLS 1.3 + optional customer KMS for at-rest. We attach a digitally signed delivery receipt (RSA signature) that binds manifest + checksum set + delivery timestamp.

3) Formats & transfer options:
   - NDJSON (default) and Parquet (optional).
   - Delivery via customer S3/Azure container (preferred), scp to on-prem gateway, or secure temporary download (presigned, single-use).

4) Legal hold / erasure interactions:
   - Legal hold is a flag in the tenant ledger; erasure requests are blocked while hold is active and the block is recorded. We can provide an auditable ledger export showing hold events.

5) Forensics and chain-of-custody add-ons:
   - Optional integrity statement and SRE-signed custody log.

Attachments included: retention-matrix.xlsx, export_manifest_template.json, sample-handoff-checklist.pdf

Next steps: please confirm the preferred delivery endpoint and whether you want unredacted archives (encrypted) or redacted extracts. If Crescent wants us to produce a Statement of Work for a one-time forensic harvest, we can produce an ETA + fixed pricing (referenced as DEAL-4532).

Best,
David Kim
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
